aspects.says: Stream.toArray() returns an Object[] that no cast turns into a String[]; String[]::new gives the stream the element type.
When a static method taking all the interface's parameters and an instance method taking all but the first both fit, javac reports the reference as ambiguous instead of choosing.
basis: section:`Class::method` Is Static or Unbound, and the Method's Declaration Decides Which

aspects.says: A bound reference fixes its receiver, so every interface argument goes to the method: suffix::concat puts the suffix in front, and the value-as-receiver form needs a lambda.
basis: section:A Bound Reference Holds Its Receiver, and the Interface's Arguments Become the Method's

aspects.says: A constructor reference takes the interface's parameters as constructor arguments, so computeIfAbsent(key, ArrayList::new) with Integer keys calls ArrayList(int initialCapacity), and a negative key throws.
basis: section:`Class::new` Picks Its Constructor From the Interface's Parameters

aspects.says: A constructor reference runs its constructor on every call, while the receiver of a bound reference such as new StringBuilder()::append is created once and shared by every call.
basis: section:A Constructor Reference Makes a New Object per Call; a Bound Reference Reuses One

aspects.says: int[]::new is an IntFunction<int[]> but does not fit Stream.toArray; a primitive array comes from IntStream.toArray().
aspects.reason: the wrong form is a compile error, so there is no running wrong solution for a test to catch

aspects.says: A record's constructor reference is its canonical constructor, with the components in order.
basis: section:`Class::new` Picks Its Constructor From the Interface's Parameters
aspects.reason: a reference that does not match the canonical constructor's components fails to compile, so no wrong solution runs for a test to catch

aspects.says: Class::method passes every interface argument to a static method, but makes the first argument the receiver of an instance method, so an unbound reference needs one more interface parameter than the method has.
basis: section:`Class::method` Is Static or Unbound, and the Method's Declaration Decides Which

aspects.says: this::m dispatches to the object's override, while super::m always runs the parent's body.
basis: section:`this::` Dispatches; `super::` Is Fixed to the Parent's Body

aspects.says: An unbound reference may name a supertype of the receiver, and the call still runs the receiver's own override.
basis: section:Through a Supertype, the Call Still Reaches the Override
